operatingCostModel.summary: Treat student co-design, cloud/platform consumption and student-facing AI inference as continuing product operating costs rather than one-off Year One discovery items. The current planning profile keeps these lines explicit and separately challengeable: paid student visioning and co-design internships at £15,000 per year; Azure, environments and platform costs ramping £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 across mobilisation and then £100,000 per year in BAU; and a provisional runtime AI inference, retrieval and token-consumption allowance of £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 across mobilisation and £100,000 per year in BAU. The AI allowance is deliberately separate from the £90,000 Devin/Cognition engineering-productivity budget held in 4.1.3.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £15,000 per year across mobilisation, £45,000 over three years in constant 2026 prices. The envelope should fund meaningful paid student participation rather than episodic consultation, with exact internship numbers, duration and payroll treatment determined through King’s employment arrangements.

newInvestment.rationale: Student partnership should remain a standing part of product discovery, prioritisation, testing and evolution after the initial Hub vision is formed. A recurring paid cohort creates continuity while broader research continues to validate representativeness.

yearlyProfile.note: Provisional Year One allowance for prototyping and first-release intelligence capability

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Provisional £225,000 three-year planning envelope using the same £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 ramp as platform costs, then £100,000 per year as a high-water BAU allowance. This is not yet a usage forecast. Jon Ward and James Costerton should validate the likely model mix, prompts and actions per active student, context and retrieval design, caching, embeddings/vector retrieval, safety and moderation, observability and any institutional AI gateway or shared capacity before the business case is finalised.
newInvestment.owner: Digital and IT with Digital Student Experience Hub product leadership
newInvestment.periodNeeded: 2026/27 onward as student-facing intelligence is introduced
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before first material student-facing AI capability is commissioned and at annual budget review
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation business case, then recurrent AI/service-consumption operating budget
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Provisional high-water allowance; Digital and IT validation required
newInvestment.rationale: The Hub architecture explicitly includes an intelligence layer. Runtime model inference and retrieval consumption are economically different from engineering-productivity tooling and from base Azure hosting, so they need a visible operating envelope rather than being assumed to be free or absorbed elsewhere.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Student-facing intelligence may be designed without a sustainable unit-cost model, creating either an unfunded live-service liability or pressure to suppress useful functionality after launch.
